plan.topic: Is CagriSema approved yet? A dated status check on the amylin + semaglutide combination
plan.angle: Spin-off of L1. Answer the status question in the first line, dated and credited to the FDA or Novo Nordisk (re-check at publish time). A filing, a committee view or an expected decision date is not approval. Then one line on what CagriSema is (semaglutide plus cagrilintide, an amylin analogue), plus one verified result with its trial, population and timeframe (REDEFINE 1, adults without diabetes, 68 weeks). Name the most common side effects (GI). Never suggest getting it outside a trial or prescription. Better route: ask your prescriber about approved options or a clinical trial. Say 'follow for more' unless L1 is already published. Prescriber line. 170 words or fewer.

package.description:
Is CagriSema approved yet? Not by the FDA as of October 2026. Novo Nordisk filed Dec 18, 2025. In REDEFINE 1, stomach side effects like nausea were more common on CagriSema (~80% vs ~40% on placebo) over 68 weeks, mostly mild to moderate.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Coadministered Cagrilintide and Semaglutide in Adults with Overweight or Obesity (REDEFINE 1), New England Journal of Medicine, June 22, 2025 — https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2502081

factcheck.summary:
I checked every claim and they're all correct.

**Status:** Novo Nordisk's own release confirms it filed a New Drug Application with the FDA on December 18, 2025. It says "The FDA is expected to review the CagriSema application in 2026." The FDA's "Novel Drug Approvals for 2026" page was current as of 10/09/2026 and doesn't list CagriSema. Recent coverage up to October 12, 2026 agrees it isn't FDA-approved yet, and secondary sources say it isn't approved in the EU either.

**REDEFINE 1 (NEJM, June 2025):** The trial enrolled adults without diabetes with a BMI of 30 or more, or 27 or more with at least one obesity-related condition. Over 68 weeks, average weight loss was 20.4% on CagriSema and 3.0% on placebo, with 2,108 people on CagriSema and 705 on placebo. The script uses the count-everyone figure, which is right; Novo's 22.7% is the on-treatment figure. Stomach side effects were 79.6% vs 39.9%, described as "mainly transient and mild-to-moderate", so "about 80% vs about 40%, mostly mild to moderate" is accurate.

**Framing and safety:** The framing is sound: it says a filing isn't approval, warns about online products without naming sellers, points viewers to a prescriber, and includes the doctor line. The hook gets answered straight away.

There are 3 minor fixes:
1. The narration is 171 words, 1 over our 170 limit.
2. The opening "no" isn't tied to a regulator.
3. The s4 on-screen stat leaves out the 68-week timeframe.

I couldn't open the NEJM page itself (it returned a 403 error). I confirmed the paper's title and numbers through NEJM's own media PDF and search results.

audio.soundNotes: Music sits right at -13.5 dB under voice (good) but pauses were a touch hot at -12.9 dB, so I trimmed overall music gain to 0.9 to bring pauses closer to the ~-14 dB ceiling while keeping the under-speech level inside the -12/-15 window. Two tick/swell cues at the shot-3 and shot-6 cuts had fallen to roughly -32 dB (likely a ducking glitch) — pushed them to the 1.5 gain cap, which helps but can't fully recover them; flag this for the next render pass. Boosted the two head-to-head stat-reveal clusters (20.4% vs 3.0% and ~80% vs ~40%) toward the -10 to -12 dB "big reveal" window since they're the story's payoff moments, and dropped one redundant swoosh layered on top of the swell/whoosh at the body-shot zoom transition to avoid clutter. Added five bespoke accents (file-stamp, soft "not approved" denial tone, two data-reveal shimmers, and a reassuring doctor-office bell) to underline the filing date, the "filing ≠ approval" caution, both stat reveals, and the "ask your prescriber" beat without adding extra loud stock hits.
